neighbours.label: ' over' as a hyphenated excess prefix in a coordinated series of verbs (over-structure, over-guide, over-…)
fire: A wise editor does not over-cut, over-polish, or over-think the draft.
The coach warned us not to over-train, over-eat, or over-sleep before the race.
Nervous cooks tend to over-salt, over-stir, and over-bake everything.
New managers often over-plan, over-report, and over-schedule their teams.
The gardener tries not to over-water, over-prune, or over-feed the roses.
Anxious parents can over-protect, over-praise, and over-direct a child.
The committee was told not to over-regulate, over-tax, or over-promise.
Young writers over-describe, over-quote, and over-qualify their claims.
quiet: A wise editor cuts, polishes, and thinks about the draft.
The coach told us to train, eat, and sleep well before the race.
Nervous cooks tend to salt, stir, and bake everything twice.
New managers often plan, report, and schedule over the weekend.
The gardener leaned over the fence to water and prune the roses.
Anxious parents watched over the child all night.
The committee argued over taxes and promises for hours.
Young writers pore over quotes and descriptions for days.

notes: Card flags broad (2.1%); top tokens ' from', ' From', ' of', ' provide', ' over', ' under' with no single token. Probes: 'do not over-explain, over-correct, or over-manage' 1.04, 'does not over-plan or over-test' 0.65; 'overestimate' 0.17, 'underachievement' 0.25, 'does not provide' 0.12, 'from Middle Dutch' 0.50 (not covered by this label).
